skill.name: realtime
skill.description: Configure ElevenAgents voice agents with ElevenLabs Realtime Mini or Max. Migrate browser apps from OpenAI Realtime and troubleshoot client secrets, WebSocket connections, and browser audio.
skill.summary: Configure ElevenLabs Realtime voice agents and migrate browser voice apps.
skill.author: elevenlabs

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown syntax or expected provider authentication, and no prompt injection was found. The source inventory can print credential-bearing lines if its file filter matches. The guide also leaves gaps in token issuance controls, microphone cleanup, transfer checks, and diagnostic logging.

remediation.issue: The source inventory prints complete matching lines.
remediation.suggestion: Use a filename-only search with separate extension filters. Inspect configuration references without displaying credential values.

remediation.issue: The client secret route has no documented access or abuse controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require an authorized app session before minting a token. Limit issuance per user, enforce short expiration, and prevent caching of token responses.

remediation.issue: Microphone acquisition starts before the cleanup handler can run.
remediation.suggestion: Protect every startup step with cleanup and release the microphone on every partial startup failure. Test these failure paths before deployment.

remediation.issue: The guide explicitly enumerates inbound transfers only after the update.
remediation.suggestion: Inventory inbound and outbound transfers before updating the agent. Test on a staging agent and confirm any production changes with the user.

remediation.issue: The verification example logs the full session creation event.
remediation.suggestion: Log only the model and voice needed for verification. Do not log full session events or credentials.

semantic_findings.title: Client Secret Route Lacks Documented Access Controls
semantic_findings.description: The migration preserves the token route without requiring authorization or issuance limits. An unprotected route could issue fresh tokens that consume the workspace's paid quota.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The browser requests a token, but the guide does not require controls on the issuing route. An existing application may already enforce them.

semantic_findings.title: Microphone Can Stay Open After Startup Failure
semantic_findings.description: The example opens the microphone before entering its cleanup handler. If playback initialization fails, startup rejects without returning a stop handle or releasing the microphone.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Playback initialization is awaited after microphone acquisition and outside the try block. A rejection there skips the documented release step.

semantic_findings.title: Inbound Transfer Inventory Is Deferred Until After Update
semantic_findings.description: The guide lists incompatible transfers as a blocker but explicitly enumerates inbound agents only after the update. A missed source can fail during live calls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The precheck fetches the target configuration, and the later verification step explicitly states that missed inbound transfers can fail mid-conversation.

semantic_findings.title: Verification Logs More Session Data Than Needed
semantic_findings.description: The example logs the entire session creation event to check two values. Depending on the payload, this can expose private session settings in browser diagnostics.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code logs the unfiltered event. The guide does not show the full returned payload, so exposure depends on the provider and logging setup.

content.value_statement: Switching voice models or providers can break publishing, agent transfers, and browser audio. This skill guides model selection, browser migration, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Compare Realtime Mini and Max for instruction complexity, latency, and workspace requirements.
Guide creation of a Realtime agent or a switch between Custom and Realtime voice modes.
Identify publishing errors caused by workflow overrides, model availability, or incompatible agent transfers.
Map legacy OpenAI Realtime session fields to the current ElevenLabs session format.
Guide server-side issuance of short-lived client secrets and browser connection over WebSocket.
Troubleshoot connection failures, microphone capture, audio playback, and interruptions.
limitations: Browser migration does not cover server-side audio relays or telephony bridges.
Realtime availability depends on the workspace, data residency, and retention settings.
The guide does not verify compatibility for functions, handoffs, guardrails, or other features beyond voice conversation.
The guide does not configure Custom mode models or cover Scribe speech-to-text and text API migrations.

use_cases.title: Choose a Model for a Voice Agent
use_cases.description: Compare Mini and Max before creating an agent. Review the workspace requirements and identify which Custom settings Realtime manages.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Browser Voice App
use_cases.description: Keep the OpenAI Realtime SDK while planning changes to token issuance, session configuration, and browser audio.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Publishing or Transfer Failure
use_cases.description: Identify workflow overrides, workspace restrictions, and incompatible voice modes before changing a live agent.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Mini and Max
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Select a model for a new voice agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Realtime Mini and Max for [agent task] in [workspace region]. List the workspace settings I should verify before choosing.

prompt_templates.title: Check an Existing Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Review compatibility before making changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted agent configuration for Realtime blockers. Check workflow overrides and transfers in both directions. Propose the smallest change without editing or publishing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Browser SDK Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Move a browser voice app from WebRTC to WebSocket.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an ElevenLabs Realtime migration for [browser framework]. Map legacy session fields and describe server token controls, browser audio, and tests. Identify features that need separate verification.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Staging Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Investigate a connection or audio failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these redacted staging logs and session settings. Distinguish workspace access, token rejection, session format, and audio problems. Propose tests for interruptions and cleanup after partial startup failures.

output_examples.input: Can I switch this voice agent to Mini if a Custom mode agent transfers callers to it?
output_examples.output: Keep the receiving agent in Custom mode for now. Identify all transfer partners and test a coordinated mode change before publishing.

output_examples.input: The browser WebSocket connects, but I hear no audio after migrating from WebRTC.
output: Check whether the app starts microphone capture and playback explicitly.
Use 24 kHz mono PCM16 for capture and playback.
Test that playback stops on interruption and the microphone closes when the session ends.

output_examples.input: The browser WebSocket closes with code 4001.
output_examples.output: Check that the server issued a fresh ElevenLabs client secret and the browser passes only its value to the session.

best_practices: Check workspace availability and every transfer partner before approving a live voice mode change.
Keep provider keys on the server and restrict short-lived token issuance to authorized users.
Test 24 kHz audio, playback interruption, and microphone release on normal exit and startup failure.
anti_patterns: Do not put a provider API key in browser code, chat, or logs.
Do not clear stored Custom settings when changing Voice mode.
Do not assume WebSocket connects the microphone and speaker automatically as WebRTC does.

faq.question: When should I choose Realtime Mini or Max?
faq.answer: Start with Mini for latency and cost. Evaluate Max for complex instructions or multi-step tool calls, subject to workspace and compliance requirements.

faq.question: Can I return an agent to Custom mode?
faq.answer: Yes. Clear the selected Realtime model to restore the stored Custom model and speech settings.

faq.question: Can I keep the OpenAI Realtime SDK?
faq.answer: Yes, for the browser migration described here. Change the token issuer, WebSocket endpoint, model, and session settings.

faq.question: Does the browser need the ElevenLabs API key?
faq.answer: No. Keep the provider key on the server and send only a short-lived client secret to the browser.

faq.question: What do WebSocket close codes 4001 and 4003 indicate?
faq.answer: The guide associates 4001 with a rejected or expired client secret and 4003 with unavailable workspace access.

faq.question: Does the skill migrate server-side audio relays?
faq.answer: No. Its migration workflow covers browser connections and does not provide steps for server relays or telephony bridges.
